metadata.topic: Cell Biology — Similarities Between Plant and Animal Cells
metadata.note: 2m: list TWO similarities between plant and animal cells. 2 slots, 1m each. Multiple correct: both have nucleus, cell membrane, cytoplasm, mitochondria, ribosomes, DNA. Distractors are features UNIQUE to plants (cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole) or UNIQUE to animals (no cell wall, no chloroplasts, centrioles).

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2023 Q1a(iii) — Two Similarities Between Plant Cell and Animal Cell

question.general_feedback:
Similarities between plant cells and animal cells:

Both types of cell contain:

  • Nucleus — contains DNA; controls cell activities
  • Cell membrane — controls what enters and leaves the cell
  • Cytoplasm — liquid medium where chemical reactions occur
  • Mitochondria — site of aerobic respiration (produces ATP)
  • Ribosomes — site of protein synthesis

NOT similarities: cell wall (plant only), chloroplasts (plant only), large central vacuole (plant only), centrioles (animal only in most cases).

options.text: Both have a large central vacuole

groups.label: First similarity between plant cell and animal cell
groups.diagnostic_hint: Both plant and animal cells are eukaryotic. Shared structures include: nucleus (contains DNA), cell membrane (controls entry/exit), cytoplasm (site of reactions), and mitochondria (energy production).

options.text: Both have a large central vacuole

groups.label: Second similarity between plant cell and animal cell (different from first)
groups.diagnostic_hint: Choose a different shared structure. Structures found ONLY in plants (cell wall, chloroplasts, large central vacuole) are NOT similarities — they are differences.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 7 tokens for 2 slots. 4 correct similarities (any 2 of 4 earn full marks). 'Cell wall' is a plant-only feature (not present in animal cells). 'Chloroplasts' are plant-only (or some protists). 'Large central vacuole' is a plant feature — animal cells have small, temporary vacuoles only. The 3 false tokens represent the three classic plant-specific structures that students may incorrectly believe both cell types share.
